title: inbox.py: handing the author's messages to a running agent
about: Task W104. The author types a message on the page or screen. A hook in the running agent session (claude, codex, kiro) or a plugin (opencode) picks it up at the agent's next tool call or stop, and the model reads it.

plugin.label: opencode's plugin
plugin.note: lives inside the agent's own process

box.label: inbox/
box.note: one .txt file per message; sorted names are sending order

delivered.label: delivered/
delivered.note: beside inbox/; a file's mtime is when it was delivered; nothing in inbox.py ever removes or empties it

msg.label: a message's state
msg.note: waiting while it is in inbox/, delivered once moved

msgfile.label: the open message file
msgfile.note: a file handle, open only while its text is read

stdin.label: the hook's input
stdin.note: JSON from the agent on stdin

agentfile.label: .kiro/agents/dfs-inbox.json
agentfile.note: written into the worktree for kiro

inbox/ cannot be listed → no messages
rename failed: another hook took it → skip, return nothing for it
read fails after the rename → the message counts as delivered and the model never gets it
a blank message is moved to delivered/ and dropped from the texts: delivered, but the model is told nothing
input is not JSON → {} → treated as the main session, which may claim
peek or ack with no DFS_INBOX → message on stderr, exit 2
a subagent's hook claims nothing, so the message waits for the main session
git or the exclude file fails → the agent file is still written, the exclude is skipped
one file per message, never a partial one
everything waiting at once, oldest first; claude, codex and kiro move it before reading (at most once)
opencode reads without moving, then ack moves (at least once: a refused prompt leaves it waiting)
two hooks at once cannot both get a file: the second rename fails
nothing waiting → the hook prints nothing and the session carries on

handled.error: kiro starting its own agent as a sub-agent
handled.how: refused, exit 2, so it cannot take the message
